A path for deeper reading

Focus the next stage of research on: Catawba-authored history, language, pottery, land and governance. The sources below are selected reading paths; their authorship, dates and community scope should guide how they are used.

Maps with context

Historical maps

Explore authentic historical documents connected to this entry. Their names and boundaries reflect their makers and periods.

c. 1721 design; LOC reproduction, 1929 · Historical community represented: Nasaw

Catawba deerskin map: archival reproduction

Unidentified Indigenous maker; colonial copy associated with Francis Nicholson

Nasaw occupies the largest central circle. LOC identifies it as a central Catawba community, making this an educational link to Catawba history and relationships rather than proof of the maker's identity.

Historical scope: Network represented around 1721; surviving copies and reproductions have separate dates.

Evidence for this connection: LOC: Catawba map interpretation ↗

Map-room record & credits ↗Original archive ↗

Underlying mapmaker and colonial copyist unnamed. Supplied digital reproduction; exact scan provenance unconfirmed. Historical interpretation: Library of Congress and Newberry Library. Archive reuse and provenance notes ↗

These map connections are a growing selection. Historical depictions do not establish current boundaries, and a link does not imply community authorship or endorsement.
